 A Tier 4 diesel engine with Scr (selective catalytic reduction) is a type of diesel engine designed to reduce emissions. It's similar to a regular diesel engine, but it has additional components to reduce nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions. The main components of a Tier 4 diesel engine with Scr include:

1. Engine block and cylinder head: The structural foundation of the engine.
2. Crankshaft, pistons, and connecting rods: The power train, where the pistons move up and down the cylinders, converting the linear motion of the pistons into rotational motion of the crankshaft.
3. Camshaft: Controls the opening and closing of the valves, which allow the air and fuel mixture to enter the cylinders and the exhaust gases to exit.
4. Turbocharger and intercooler: Increase the efficiency of the engine by compressing the air before it enters the cylinders and cooling the compressed air after it exits.
5. Exhaust treatment system: Reduces the emissions of nitrogen oxides by converting them into nitrogen and water.
6. Selective catalytic reduction system (Scr): Uses a reductant, such as ammonia, to reduce the nitrogen oxides into nitrogen and water.
7. Aftertreatment components: These include diesel oxidation catalyst (DOC), diesel particulate filter (DPF), and ammonia slip catalyst (ASC), which are part of the exhaust treatment system.
